comparisonVerdict.rationale: Both samples communicate a complete runner loop with readable input and a deliberate low-poly presentation. One favors title and obstacle readability; the other favors cleaner HUD hierarchy and a more detailed runner model. Neither frame shows sound or particle feedback, so the polish result is a tie rather than an inferred winner.

samples.biggestGap: No visible moment-to-moment effects, particles, or audio feedback.
samples.evidence: The active run is immediately readable through the road, collectibles, obstacle, player, HUD, and input strip.
samples.label: sample-01

samples.biggestGap: The world is polished but the player and obstacles could read larger at the same camera distance.
samples.evidence: The active run has clear lane, jump, slide, score, distance, speed, collectible, obstacle, and environment cues.
samples.label: sample-02
